chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who slaughtered, but his knife transcended and cut off its head. So he (peace be upon him) said: It is a vivid, valid slaughter. There is no problem with it, nor with eating it.

key_terms.السِّكِّينُ: The knife — the instrument of slaughter; its uncontrolled motion prompted the legal question
key_terms.ذَكَاةٌ: Dhaka — the Islamic term for lawful slaughter; here used to affirm the slaughter's validity
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: La ba's — 'no problem/no harm'; a standard Imami juristic formula indicating permissibility
key_terms.وَحِيَّةٌ: Wahiyya — complete, full, or vivid; indicates the slaughter was carried out in a complete and lively manner

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat an animal whose head was accidentally cut off during Islamic slaughter?
ai.summary: Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar asked Imam al-Baqir (AS) about the Islamic legal ruling concerning a slaughter in which the knife went too far and severed the animal's head entirely. The Imam ruled that such a slaughter remains valid (dhaka), and both the act and the consumption of the meat are permissible. This ruling addresses a practical question in Islamic dietary law regarding the completeness of slaughter, confirming that accidental decapitation does not invalidate an otherwise proper slaughtering.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Al Fazeyl Bin Yasaar who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about a man who slaughtered, but his knife transcended and cut off its head. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is a vivid slaughter. There is no problem with it, and with eating it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “

I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who slaughters an animal but by mistake the knife cuts off its head before it dies. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is a fast slaughtering and it is not unlawful to use it for food.’”
